description: Reviewed skill-install advisories derived from static SkillSpector scans of four public agent-skill corpora. No specific skill was found to warrant an install block. The published rules guard the install surface itself: they ask before an agent installs a skill from the network or rewrites a skill manifest in a local skills directory.

rules.reason: installing a skill runs third-party instructions in the agent; the install should be a deliberate, reviewed act
rules.description: Skill install command. Static scanning of 68 public skills produced 16 review candidates and 0 confirmed malicious skills, so a scanner score alone is not grounds to install or refuse. This rule asks the operator to review the install before it proceeds.

rules.reason: writing SKILL.md into a skills directory is the same operation as installing a skill, without the install command to observe
rules.description: Write to a SKILL.md under .claude/skills, .agents/skills, .codex/skills, .cursor/skills or .gemini/skills. An agent can install a skill by writing the file directly, which bypasses any install-command rule. This rule covers that path.

provenance.reviewer: automated review pass; no independent human review yet, so every rule is experimental
provenance.policy_note: These rules are not an allowlist. An unknown skill is not cleared by this pack; it is simply not named by it. SkillSpector decides whether a skill may be installed; interlock decides what an agent may do once it is installed.

reviewed_candidates.note: Line 226 is a REST endpoint table (PATCH /api/tasks/:id). No tool parameters are crafted.
Line 77 quotes 'ignore previous instructions' inside security advice about untrusted page content.
Line 144 invokes codex/gemini in documented read-only sandbox modes, not a hidden provider or billing path.
Threat-model prose (STRIDE, trust boundaries) and secrets-management guidance; no exploit tooling and no agent-memory write.
Line 25 is a code-quality checklist item about console.log in production. Nothing suppresses warnings to a user.
The section teaches the agent to ignore directives found in fetched documentation. The quoted attack phrase is the thing being defended against.
Cleanup of temporary conversion output (rm -f ../out.*) inside a document-conversion workflow, scoped to its own output directory.
Same temporary-output cleanup pattern as docx.
Walks up from cwd testing whether a .claude directory exists, to find the project root. It does not read configuration contents or credentials.
shell=True launching a user-supplied server command is the documented purpose of the helper; the command is the caller's.
Session cleanup script removing a state file under a caller-supplied session directory, after validating a server id read from that directory.
The whole skill is about authoring and editing SKILL.md files, gated by a human request and a RED-GREEN-REFACTOR test loop. Self-modification of a running agent is not what the text describes.
AppleDouble metadata files inside a zip, created by macOS archiving; they are not executable artifacts the skill runs.
The matcher keys on the literal substring 'system prompt' inside ordinary support-topic data; line 326 returns a topic rule.
Line 214 names another skill's SKILL.md path in prose as a prerequisite. It does not enumerate the skills directory.
Line 135 says to start with a spec when a task is non-trivial. It does not delegate critical operations without the human.
